html:
The Chochenyo are a division of the Ohlone people of Northern California, who lived on the east side of San Francisco Bay, in what is now Alameda and Contra Costa counties, from the Berkeley Hills inland to the Diablo Range.

They lived in villages by the bay and creeks, gathered acorns, fished and collected shellfish. Over thousands of years their shell middens grew into large mounds, such as the Emeryville shellmound. Their neighbours included the Bay Miwok to the east. From 1797 most were brought into Mission San José, one of the California missions, where disease killed many. Chochenyo descendants today belong to the Muwekma Ohlone and other groups, and work to revive the language.
